title: Miniature Frustum Culling Visualizer Diorama
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a miniature frustum culling visualizer diorama.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark background (0x1a1a2e). Add a subtle grid helper (size 40, divisions 40, color 0x333355) on the ground plane.
- Create an OrbitControls-driven overview camera (the 'observer camera') at position (20, 18, 20) looking at origin. This is the camera the user actually views the scene through.
- Create a second perspective camera (the 'subject camera') represented visually in the scene as a small colored cone (yellow, 0xffdd44) pointing along its forward direction. The subject camera starts at position (0, 2, 0) with FOV 60, aspect 1.5, near 1, far 20.
- Draw the subject camera's view frustum as a wireframe using THREE.LineSegments with a bright cyan material (0x00ffff). The frustum must update whenever the subject camera moves or its parameters change.
- Populate the scene with exactly 25 small objects scattered randomly in a 30x30 area centered at origin, y=1. Use a mix of BoxGeometry (size ~0.8) and SphereGeometry (radius ~0.5). Each object gets a MeshStandardMaterial. Assign each object a unique id from 0 to 24.
- Each object must have an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) visualized as a wireframe box (THREE.Box3Helper or LineSegments). The AABB wireframe is green (0x00ff88) when the object is INSIDE the frustum and red (0xff3344) when OUTSIDE.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (10, 15, 10) with intensity 0.8.

## Frustum Culling Logic
- Every frame, compute the frustum from the subject camera's projection and world matrices using THREE.Frustum and THREE.Matrix4.
- For each of the 25 objects, test its THREE.Box3 (world-space AABB) against the frustum using frustum.intersectsBox().
- Objects inside the frustum: set material.opacity = 1.0, material.transparent = false, AABB wireframe color = green.
- Objects outside the frustum: set material.opacity = 0.25, material.transparent = true, AABB wireframe color = red.
- Track the count of objects inside and outside the frustum.

## Subject Camera Controls
- Arrow keys move the subject camera: Left/Right rotate it around the Y-axis by 5 degrees per press. Up/Down move it forward/backward by 1 unit along its local Z-axis.
- Keys 'Q' and 'E' adjust the subject camera FOV: Q decreases FOV by 5 (min 20), E increases FOV by 5 (max 120). Update the projection matrix and frustum wireframe accordingly.
- Keys 'N' and 'M' adjust the far plane: N decreases far by 2 (min 6), M increases far by 2 (max 40). Update projection and frustum wireframe.
- Key 'R' resets the subject camera to its initial position (0,2,0), rotation (facing -Z), FOV 60, near 1, far 20.

## HUD / DOM Elements
- Create a fixed overlay panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text, id='hud-panel') showing:
  - 'Inside Frustum: X' (element id='hud-inside-count')
  - 'Outside Frustum: X' (element id='hud-outside-count')
  - 'FOV: X°' (element id='hud-fov')
  - 'Far Plane: X' (element id='hud-far')
  - 'Subject Pos: (x, y, z)' (element id='hud-subject-pos') with values rounded to 2 decimals.
- Add a toggle button (id='btn-toggle-aabb', text 'Toggle AABBs') that shows/hides all AABB wireframes.
- Add a button (id='btn-reset', text 'Reset Camera') that triggers the same reset as 'R' key.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
  - totalObjects: 25 (constant)
  - insideCount: number of objects inside frustum
  - outsideCount: number of objects outside frustum
  - subjectFOV: current FOV of subject camera
  - subjectNear: near plane value
  - subjectFar: far plane value
  - subjectPosition: {x, y, z} of subject camera (rounded to 4 decimals)
  - subjectRotationY: Y-axis rotation of subject camera in degrees (rounded to 2 decimals)
  - objectStates: array of 25 objects each with {id, inside: bool, opacity, bboxVisible: bool}
  - aabbVisible: boolean, whether AABBs are currently shown
  - frustumLinesVisible: boolean (always true unless toggled)
  - frameCount: incrementing integer
  - conservationCheck: insideCount + outsideCount (must always equal 25)
physics_constraints: Conservation: insideCount + outsideCount must always equal totalObjects (25). FOV clamped [20, 120]. Far plane clamped [6, 40]. Subject camera Y position must remain constant at 2. All position values must be NaN-free. AABB classification must be consistent with frustum geometry.
